concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: חמישה כנפי ראה — mentioned explicitly as a distinct concept: 'ובהתורה יש חמישה ספרים כנגד חמישה כנפי ראה' (Tikkun 25). This is a sub-specification of the ראה node already in Package 1. The bechina 'five wings of the lung = five books of Torah' is structurally captured by the edge תורה ↔ ראה (id 2652). A standalone node 'חמישה כנפי ראה' could be added to further granulate Package 1, but its essential nature is already covered; no missing bechina equivalence is absent from the packages.

אלישע — cited as an exemplar ('כמו שכתוב באלישע כשהחיה את בן השונמית') but not placed in a bechina relationship. He illustrates the eitza chain (man-movement → revival of dead) but is not declared a bechina of any concept in this Torah.
בן השונמית — mentioned as the recipient of resurrection; narrative reference only, no bechina.

חמימות / חמימות שבלב — the heat/warmth of the heart, mentioned as 'החמימות שבלב' and 'רוגזו של יוסף הינו החמימות שבלב'. This concept is functionally equivalent to אש/דין (Package 3) within this Torah — the burning heat of the heart is the fire/dinin. However, it appears as a descriptive phrase rather than a node equated via bechina to another concept. It is subsumed by the אש ↔ דין bechina already in Package 3.

ניע וניד / נע ונד — the motion of walking back and forth ('ויילך אחת הנה ואחת הנה') is the action through which the Torah-man accomplishes the cooling. This is the mechanism (eitza) rather than a bechina identity. Not a bechina node.
מתים / להחיות מתים — reviving the dead is the miraculous outcome of the teaching; it appears as the end-point of the eitza chain. No bechina statement links it to any concept in this Torah.
analysis_notes.torah_summary: Torah #92 is structurally complete in the dataset. All seven bechina edges map to one of three clean connected components: (1) the good cluster of Torah-Truth-Lung-Jacob-Man (Package 1, 5 nodes), (2) the neutral heart-Joseph cluster (Package 2, 2 nodes), and (3) the evil fire-judgment cluster (Package 3, 2 nodes). The source text contains no bechina language that is missing from the dataset. The eitza chain (man-movement → cools fire → revives dead) operates between the packages but is correctly classified as eitza, not bechina. The teaching has a clear three-package architecture: the good force (Torah/Jacob/lung) overcomes the evil force (fire/dinin) by cooling the structural container (heart/Joseph) that holds the fire.
